# v1.1.0-dev.85 — The dialogs fill their windows, this time for real

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.84`.

## The Fix dev.84 Said It Made

dev.85 exists mostly because dev.84 claimed to make dialog content fill its
window and only managed it for one dialog out of several.

The rule it shipped named five parts of the app by hand. Three of those
five names did not exist anywhere in the markup. A style rule aimed at
something that is not there does not complain. It silently did nothing for
the dialogs that needed it. The one dialog that happened to be named
correctly got fixed. That was also the only one anyone looked at.

The History list sat above 294 pixels of empty window. Load details had
269. Both are zero now.

What is different this time is not the fix. It is that there is a measure
for it. A check reads whatever a dialog actually contains, rather than
whatever a rule claims it contains, and reports the gap between the last
piece of content and the buttons. It was run before the change and after,
and the same check now fails if anyone writes a rule aimed at a part of the
app that is not there.

## Change Several Monitors Together

The display editor let you pick one monitor at a time. Setting the same
scaling on three of them meant doing it three times.

The picker takes a selection now, the same way the visual editor takes one:
**Ctrl+click** adds or removes a monitor, **Shift+click** takes the run
between two. Every selected monitor gets its own card, which keeps
anything from hiding behind the group. A strip above them applies a setting to all of
them at once.

Scaling there is **step up** or **step down** rather than a percentage.
Every display has its own ladder of supported scales, and 150% is not
necessarily a rung on all of them. A step moves one rung along whatever
ladder each display actually has, worked out per display.

## The Resolution Search Moved Into The List

dev.84 put a filter box next to the resolution dropdown. It works. It also
sits outside the thing it filters, which is not where anyone looks for it.

Open the resolution list now and the search is the first thing in it, above
the sizes, the way most searchable dropdowns do it. The shape headings stay
put as you narrow it down. Arrow keys, Home, End, Enter and Escape all do
what they should. A query that matches nothing says so, rather than
leaving one row that has nothing to do with what you typed.

Underneath, the list is still an ordinary dropdown with an ordinary value.
That is deliberate. Everything else in the editor goes on reading it the
way it always did, which is what keeps a change like this from quietly
breaking the parts nobody thought to check.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
